song_story.overview: Palette was released in 2017 as the title track of IU's mini-album of the same name, timed to her 25th birthday. The song is IU looking back at who she used to be — the things she thought she liked, the person she performed for others — and noticing how much has quietly changed now that she's more comfortable being herself. G-Dragon appears not as a romantic feature but as a real-life senior figure in the industry, addressing her by her actual name, Ji-eun, and mentioning his own age (thirty) — the collaboration itself becomes part of the song's theme about time passing and settling into yourself.
song_story.cultural_root: The song is built around 나이듦 (getting older) and 스물다섯 (twenty-five) as a specifically meaningful Korean age milestone — old enough to have shed some youthful self-consciousness, still young enough that people around you will insist you're not really an adult yet. IU repeats 이제 조금 알 것 같아 날 ('I think I'm starting to understand myself a little now') — not a dramatic transformation, just the ordinary, gradual process of figuring out your own taste instead of performing someone else's.

verse_1.lines: 이상하게도 요즘엔isanghagedo yojeumen / 그냥 쉬운 게 좋아geunyang swiun ge joa / 하긴 그래도hagin geuraedo / 여전히 코린 음악은 좋더라yeojeonhi korin eumageun joteora / Hot pink보다 진한 보라색을 더 좋아해Hot pinkboda jinhan borasaegeul deo joahae / 또 뭐더라 단추 있는 pajamas, lipsticktto mwodeora danchu inneun pajamas, lipstick
verse_1.literal: Strangely enough, these days / I just like things that are easy / then again / I still like corny music / I like deep purple more than hot pink
verse_1.context: 코린 (a slangy pronunciation of 촌스러운/'corny,' or possibly referencing 'corn') paired with 하긴 그래도 ('but then again') shows her noticing her own contradictions without needing to resolve them — she doesn't have to have consistent, sophisticated taste to know it's genuinely hers.

chorus_1.lines: 좀 짓궂은 장난들jom jitgujeun jangnandeul / 날 좋아하는 거 알아nal joahaneun geo ara / 이제 조금 알 것 같아 날ije jogeum al geot gata nal / 긴 머리보다gin meoriboda / 반듯이 자른 단발이 좋아bandeusi jareun danbari joa / 하긴 그래도 좋은 날 부를 땐hagin geuraedo joeun nal bureul ttaen
chorus_1.literal: I like it, I'm twenty-five / I know that I like myself / I got this, I'm truly fine / I think I'm starting to understand myself a little now
chorus_1.context: 날 좋아하는 거 알아 — 'I know [I] like myself' — is a quiet but significant claim of self-acceptance rather than self-love as a performance. 조금 (a little) keeps the claim modest and believable rather than a sudden epiphany.

verse_2.lines: 참 예뻤더라cham yeppeotdeora / 오 왜 그럴까 조금 촌스러운 걸 좋아해?o wae geureolkka jogeum chonseureoun geol joahae? / 그림보다 빼곡히 채운 palettegeurimboda ppaegoki chae-un palette / 일기 잠들었던 시간들ilgi jamdeureotdeon sigandeul / 날 미워하는 거 알아nal miwohaneun geo ara / 이제 조금 알 것 같아 날ije jogeum al geot gata nal
verse_2.literal: More than long hair / I like a neatly cut bob / then again, when I wore it long on good days / it really was pretty
verse_2.context: 예뻤더라 uses -더라, a grammar form for reporting a personal, remembered observation — she's looking back at old photos or memories almost like a third party, noting objectively that the old version of herself looked good too, without needing to reject that past self to embrace the current one.

chorus_2.lines: 어려서 모든 게 어려워eoryeoseo modeun ge eoryeowo / 잔소리에 매 서러워jansorie mae seoreowo / 꾸중만 듣던 철부지 애kkujungman deutdeon cheolbuji ae / 겨우 스무고개 넘어gyeou seumugogae neomeo / 기쁨도 잠시 어머?gippeumdo jamsi eomeo? / 아프니까 웬 청춘이래apeunikka wen cheongchunirae
chorus_2.literal: I like it, I'm twenty-five / I know that people/I dislike me / I got this, I'm truly fine / I think I'm starting to understand myself a little now
chorus_2.context: The second chorus swaps 좋아하는 (liking) for 미워하는 (disliking/resenting) — could mean other people dislike her, or that she still sometimes dislikes herself. The ambiguity is likely intentional: at 25, both kinds of criticism (external and internal) exist, and she's naming that she's still fine either way.

gdragon_verse.lines: 지은아 오빠는 말이야 지금 막 서른인데jieuna oppaneun mariya jigeum mak seoreuninde / 나는 절대로 아니야 근데 막 어른이 돼naneun jeoldaero aniya geunde mak eoreuni dwae / 아직도 한참 멀었는데ajikdo hancham meoreonneunde / 너보다 다섯 살 밖에 안 먹었는데neoboda daseot sal bakke an meogeonneunde / 스물 위 서른 아래 고맘때, right thereseumul wi seoreun arae gomamttae, right there / 애도 어른도 아닌 나이 때 그저 나일 때aedo eoreundo anin nai ttae geujeo nail ttae
gdragon_verse.literal: Ji-eun, listen, oppa just turned thirty / I'm absolutely not [old], but I'm somehow becoming an adult / even though I still have a long way to go / even though I'm only five years older than you
gdragon_verse.context: G-Dragon calls IU by her real given name, 지은 (Ji-eun), which is a genuine, unusual moment of the song breaking the fourth wall — this is two real industry colleagues, not characters. 오빠 is how a woman addresses an older male friend/relative, and here he's using it about himself in third person, a common way Korean speakers refer to themselves when talking to someone younger. His verse mirrors hers: even at thirty he doesn't feel fully 'adult' either.

gdragon_verse_2.lines: 가장 찬란하게 빛이 나gajang challanhage bichi na / 어둠이 드리워질 때도 겁내지 마eodumi deuriwojil ttaedo geomnaeji ma / 너무 아름다워서 꽃잎 활짝 펴서neomu areumdawoseo kkochip hwaljjak pyeoseo / 언제나 사랑받는 아이 youeonjena sarangbanneun ai you / Palette, 일기, 잠들었던 시간들Palette, ilgi, jamdeureotdeon sigandeul / 날 좋아하는 거 알아nal joahaneun geo ara / 이제 조금 알 것 같아 날ije jogeum al geot gata nal / (아직 할 말이 많아)(ajik hal mari mana) / 날 미워하는 거 알아nal miwohaneun geo ara / 이제 조금 알 것 같아 날ije jogeum al geot gata nal
gdragon_verse_2.literal: That in-between stage, above twenty, below thirty, right there / the age that's neither a kid nor an adult, just being yourself / you shine the most brilliantly / even when darkness falls over you, don't be afraid
gdragon_verse_2.context: 고맘때 is a colloquial way of saying 'right around that time/age.' 애도 어른도 아닌 나이 — 'the age that's neither child nor adult' — names the specific in-between-ness of the mid-twenties directly, and 그저 나일 때 (just when you're simply yourself) reframes that ambiguity as the actual peak, not a stage to rush past.

artist_context: IU (Lee Ji-eun) writes and produces much of her own catalog and released Palette as a birthday reflection on turning 25, a milestone commonly treated in Korea as the shift from young adulthood toward a more settled identity. G-Dragon, leader of BIGBANG, appears as a real mentor figure in Korean music rather than a romantic collaborator, which is part of what makes the verse land as sincere rather than as a typical duet.
honorific_level: informal — 반말 in IU's verses; G-Dragon uses 오빠 self-reference, casual and warm

grammar_highlights.usage: 'I noticed/recall that ~.' 예뻤더라 — reporting a personal memory as an observation, common in reflective lyrics.
'I think/feel like ~.' 알 것 같아 — a soft, tentative claim about self-knowledge rather than a definitive statement.
다섯 살 밖에 안 먹었는데 — 'even though I'm only five years older' — 밖에 always pairs with a negative verb to mean 'nothing but, only.'
